name: Melbourne Beach
seat: Melbourne Beach (a town in Brevard County)

officials.name: A. Marie Smith
officials.note: Appointed by the Town Commission; prepared the FY2027 budget.

quorum_court.source: Melbourne Beach is a council-manager town: five elected commissioners (one serves as Mayor, one as Vice Mayor) set policy and adopt the budget and tax rate, and an appointed Town Manager runs operations. Town Hall is at 507 Ocean Avenue. The town sits inside Brevard County, which has its own Board of County Commissioners, sheriff, and jail.

election_office.name: Brevard County Supervisor of Elections
election_office.early_voting: Oct. 19–31: Monday–Friday 8 am to 6 pm, Saturday–Sunday 8 am to 4 pm, at any of four sites — Melbourne (1515 Sarno Rd), Palm Bay (450 Cogan Dr SE), Viera (2725 Judge Fran Jamieson Way), and Titusville (400 South St). Mail ballots can be dropped at secure intake stations at these sites during early-voting hours.
election_office.election_day: On Election Day you vote at your assigned precinct — find it on votebrevard.gov or your voter card.

races.office: Town of Melbourne Beach — Mayor (three-year term)
races.note: One candidate qualified, and the Supervisor of Elections lists the race as unopposed. The four commission seats are not up this year. Whether an unopposed race still appears on the ballot is up to state law and the town — your sample ballot will show it.

budget_adoption_window.note: Florida towns hold budget workshops in early summer, then two public hearings in September under the state’s Truth in Millage (TRIM) law; the fiscal year begins October 1. Melbourne Beach approved FY2027 on September 16, 2026.

meetings.schedule: Regular meetings monthly (schedule posted on the town site)

election_blackouts.note: Bright lines: no candidate issues, no active-ballot-measure issues, no named-individual conduct issues. The town’s $5.0 million General Obligation bond and Florida Amendment 3 are on the November 3, 2026 ballot — this site gives facts on both and opens no vote on either.
